packs.title: Desert to Sky
packs.promise: Meet Tucson from the Sonoran desert floor to the forests of a sky island.

q.s: Turn three wildly different cactus silhouettes into a desert cast of characters.
st: Choose a signed trail, visitor-center route, or legal scenic pullout in either district.
Find three saguaros with clearly different silhouettes without leaving the permitted route.
Photograph, sketch, or describe each one and give every character a short personality caption.

q.s: Build a three-part sensory map of a desert canyon shaped by rare water.
st: Choose the visitor area, an accessible route, or a permitted Crawler stop.
Notice three changing signals: sound, movement, temperature, texture, light, or water.
Turn them into a three-part canyon map using words, sketches, or private photographs.

q.t: The White Dove of the Desert
q.s: Find the white landmark that still serves the community it was built to serve.
st: Approach quietly and check whether a service, ceremony, or community activity is underway.
From a permitted public area, notice two architectural details without requiring an interior photograph.
Read onsite interpretation and save one fact about the Mission's continuing relationship with the Wa:k community.

packs.title: Streetcar & Side Streets
packs.promise: Meet Tucson block by block without building the day around a car.

q.t: The Avenue Born from an Underpass
q.s: Read one Tucson street through its older bones, streetcar rails, and present-day personality.
st: Walk one comfortable public block and find an older facade or district-history detail.
Add one streetcar detail and one contemporary piece of local art, design, or street life.
Name the three-image or three-note collection Fourth Avenue: Then, Moving, Now.

q.s: Turn Tucson's streetcar stations into one moving public-art exhibition.
st: Ride Sun Link through at least three districts, or choose a shorter ride that works for you.
Notice three different station artworks from the platform or vehicle without delaying boarding.
Give the three works a shared exhibition title.

q.s: Find the Tucson bridge that turns a practical crossing into a giant desert animal.
st: Reach the bridge using a route and travel mode appropriate for you.
Cross legally while noticing the artwork as three parts: head, body, and tail.
Turn the crossing into a three-panel sketch, photo sequence, or written creature story.
